motors.description: 200 mm spoke-PM (24s / 28p), wire 6.5x0.8, 15 wires/slot, magnet 21.33 — the working motor (I=150 A, 466.7 Hz, 2000 rpm).
motors.gamma_frame: UNKNOWN -- gamma unchanged since catalog commit 7c16693 (2026-06-07), i.e. written in the legacy 108 deg frame, but NOT re-annotated: preset '200_mm' is not in config/motor_presets.json, so this machine's d-axis cannot be calibrated
motors.gamma_frame_action: Calibrate this machine's d-axis, then shift gamma by (108 - DAXIS). For its 24s/28p topology the measured DAXIS is 60.0 deg on the 100 mm cross-section, which would make it +48 deg -- not applied, because that is an inference from another machine, not a measurement of this one.

motors.name: 100 mm · 24s/28p mid-torque
motors.description: 100 mm spoke-PM inrunner, 24 slots / 28 poles. 6.0 N·m, 2.39 kW @ 3 800 rpm, 93.1 % eff (FEM) at 46 A, 29.4 V phase-peak — fits the 14-cell (≈50 V) bus. OPTIMIZED: teeth widened 5.0→6.5 mm to relieve saturation + 10 turns of thicker wire → +2.8 pp efficiency vs the first cut, same torque & voltage. F45SH magnets, JFE 20JNEH1200 steel. MTPA γ=+12° (legacy frame: -36°).

protocol.mesh_size_rule: 1.4 mm * D/150, clamped [0.5, 2.0]; solver auto-refines to min(slot,tooth)/2; gap resolved by gap_layers=2 per half-gap

reference_provenance.caveat: The winding source is normalised by the slot's real copper area, so this run was excited at exactly n_wires*I ampere-turns (k = 1). legacy_ampere_turn_scale_k is how far this entry's PREVIOUS reference numbers were off: the old T_avg_maxwell and ripple % over-read by that factor. T_avg is still the energy/flux-linkage mean; what is left between it and T_avg_maxwell is the sliding-band Maxwell residual - see docs/SOLVER_TRIALS_2026-07-30.md, F4+F5 (fixed).
reference_provenance.gamma_frame_caveat: This reference run used gamma = -36 deg read in the CALIBRATED d-axis frame, which is neither the legacy point that number named nor the re-annotated gamma_deg = +12 deg. The reference_* fields are at a different operating point until re-measured (2026-07-31 10:54).

motors.gamma_frame: q-axis at gamma=0, d-axis auto-calibrated per machine (fem_solver_2d._resolve_daxis_shift); d3ab7cb and later

gamma_reannotation.frame: q-axis at gamma=0, d-axis auto-calibrated per machine (fem_solver_2d._resolve_daxis_shift); d3ab7cb and later

gamma_reannotation.calibration_converged: 24/24 frames, 0 Newton fallbacks, worst residual 9.98e-08 against tol 1e-3, 117.4 s
gamma_reannotation.note: Same PHYSICAL current angle, relabelled. The stored number was written when every solve used DAXIS = 108 deg; this machine's calibrated d-axis is 60 deg, so gamma moves by +48 deg to keep the operating point where it was.

pwm.bridge_model: ideal two-level bridge — no dead time, no device conduction or switching loss; a real inverter adds its own watts on top of these

coarse_bias.source: solver guard calibration, 40 mm at 16.7 kHz: 4.4 samples per carrier against 21.8 — the coarse pass reads LOW on every ripple-driven number, never high

caveats: the deltas are PWM minus a sine baseline solved at the SAME step count — an unmatched baseline reported roughly double the iron delta on the CIANO14 (1.80 W against 0.90 W)

the solver's mixed-resolution PWM settling is on, which carries a measured +1 to +2 pp bias on the reported TORQUE RIPPLE (the loss terms are unaffected, <=0.2 %).  Set SB_PWM_COARSE_SETTLE=0 for a ripple-critical measurement
ideal bridge: no dead time, no device conduction or switching loss — an inverter's own watts are not in these numbers

fit.method: log-log slope of each delta against the MEASURED ripple current, from the rated point solved at two carriers

I_ripple_law_check.note: I_ripple ∝ V_bus/(f_sw·L): halving the carrier should double the ripple current.  A measured ratio far from the prediction means the coarse pass is averaging the ripple away at the higher carrier

pair_resolution.note: the two carriers were solved at 4.6 and 4.6 samples per carrier; the coarser one under-reads its ripple-driven losses, so an exponent fitted across a large mismatch is biased LOW

envelope.note: outside this box the deltas are an extrapolation of a two-point power law — the tuner clamps to the edge and says so rather than quoting the extrapolation
